text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - British shares ushered in the new month with a 0.5 percent drop as investors fretted over the strength in sterling and rising interest rates, yet many traders and strategists said they still hold out hope for a year end rally. The FTSE 100 index of leading stocks ended 19.5 points lower at 4,038.5, as decliners beat advancers by a margin of about two to one. Second-liners fared a little better.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended bourse dealings at a record close on Monday, continuing the rally started last week, with the market boosted by a firmer dollar and strength on Wall Street. The DAX index hit a new bourse record of 2,860.24 points in early trade, before paring gains slightly to close up 13.08 points, or 0.46 percent, at 2,858.60 points. Later the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index stood at 2853.46 up 4.62 points.

PARIS - French shares closed firmer, rebounding from their morning consolidation. Traders said strength in bonds and hopes of interest rate cuts in France and Germany as early as this week gave reasons to be cheerful for Paris equities, which shrugged off a decline on Wall Street. Hopes are also high for big flows from cash-rich U.S. funds in the New Year. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 2.97 points or 0.13 percent at 2,318.63 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,322 from 2,319 on Friday's close.

ZURICH - A massive slump by two big banks und major utilities pulled Swiss shares down after a restructuring in the Swiss utility sector was announced over the weekend. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) plunged under the psychologically important level of 3,900 points. Dealers said opening losses on Wall Street aggravated the market's sluggish performance,although some stocks were buoyed by the firming U.S. dollar. The SMI ended down 28.5 points, or 0.73 percent, to 3,874.0. The all-share SPI fell 13.43 points to 2,478.78.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei 225 average tumbled on Monday as a recent boom in blue-chip issues slowed, driving dealers to unload long positions. Brokers expected the Nikkei to seek the bottom of recent range-bound trading. The Nikkei 225 ended down 345.67 points or 1.64 percent at 20,674.69.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Monday as a decline in the U.S. long bond yield gave prices a lift and market optimism kept selling interest at a minimum. The Hang Seng index ended up 123.63 points at 13,517.56, its session high. Turnover was HK$7.38 billion.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended slightly weaker but off their lows on Monday with the resource sector pinned down by a strong Australian dollar. The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries Index, closed 3.5 points lower at 2,385.1, well off its intra-day low of 2,372.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares returned to just below their previous closing levels at the end of trade on Monday after a day of choppy dealings. The gold index finished 0.7 points weaker at 1,523.4. The industrial index finished 4.7 points down at 7,992.8, after at one stage being up over 35 points.
